data.gender_notes: Else is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old Norse ‘els’, meaning ‘elf’ or ‘goddess’. In Norse mythology, elves were supernatural beings believed to inhabit the woods and forests, possessing magical powers and able to shape-shift at will. The name Else carries the meaning “Elf, goddess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Else usually hope their child will grow to embody elf, goddess and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Else total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Else" could potentially evoke a sense of connection to old Norse folklore, with its roots in the mythology of ancient Europe. It may suggest an appreciation for the natural world, as elves in Norse tales were believed to live in harmony with forest and wildlife. This could make for an intriguing and unique name for those who value the history and traditions of ancient cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name "Else" could symbolize the idea of finding harmony and connection with the natural world, as well as the idea of being guided and protected by supernatural beings, whether that be through personal interpretation or through the lens of Norse mythology. It may also serve as a reminder of the magical and enchanting qualities inherent within the world around us.
